To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maintenance energy requirements are lower in older than in younger broilers and Leghorn chickens, but the differences are small; the efficiency of energy use above maintenance is higher in younger than in older Leghorn chickens; the efficiency of use of energy above maintenance is higher for broilers than for Leghorn chickens; and the efficiency of energy usage is not related to the percentage fat gain in either broilers or Leghorn chickens.
(1) the efficiency of energy gain is higher in broilers than Leghorns and (2) the efficiency of utilization of energy above maintenance is lower in older Leghorns than in younger Leghorns.
the efficiency of energy use for gain is lower in older than younger Leghorns, but not broilers, and that the efficiency of gain in Leghorns is correlated with percentage fat gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on the utilization of energy for maintenance, gain in body weight and gain in body fat in chickens of two genotypes.
the effects of genetic selection for increased growth rate on the utilization of metabolizable energy by chickens.
the effects of age on maintenance requirements and on energetic efficiency of gain in broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the efficiency of energy use in the maintenance of Leghorns and broilers is the same, and that in the older Leghorn, the efficiency of utilization of energy for gain is lower than in the older broiler.
the efficiency of energy use above maintenance was higher in the younger birds and that this was associated with a higher percentage fat gain.

the energy utilization for maintenance and gain was not affected by age in broilers, whereas the energy utilization for gain was reduced by age in Leghorns, and that this was correlated with a reduced efficiency of fat utilization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy efficiency of Leghorns is lower than that of broilers and decreases with age, whereas the efficiency of energy use in broilers is constant with age.
the efficiency of energy use in broilers is not influenced by age, but the efficiency of energy gain in Leghorns is influenced by age.
Leghorns have a lower maintenance energy requirement, a lower efficiency of utilization of energy above maintenance, but a higher efficiency of energy utilization for fat gain than broilers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maintenance energy requirement of Leghorns is lower than that of broilers and that the efficiency of energy conversion to gain above maintenance is lower in the older Leghorn birds.
the efficiency of energy conversion to gain in broilers does not change with age, whereas it decreases in Leghorns.
the energy requirement for maintenance is not a function of age, but the efficiency of energy use is.
